title: Janax y Razar: un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador propios para un razonamiento artificial que piensa con melodías
description:
Janax is a hand-written operating system, language and assembler (all in assembly, no third-party engines) built to host Razar, an artificial reasoning system whose single judge is compression (two-part MDL). Version 0.83 (versions follow prime numbers), the gears. A program is not eaten whole: it is taken apart. With her own judge, a gear is a jump-free piece of code that the program repeats and that, said once and named, saves bits (n(L-1)-L instructions); registers are named by order of use, so the same work with other registers is the same gear. Applied to Luma's own body it finds, unprompted, legible pieces: add one, subtract one, sign, times eight, shift right. The gears that only compute on registers go into her house, and in a recipe they are lenses of her eye: her reader has a small sixteen-register machine that runs the gear's instructions on every look before it is mixed into the frame. Real program code, taken apart, running inside a recipe she writes, as data: nothing is rebuilt. Measured on the New Testament: a lens built from a gear of her own body (shift right by 8) lifts the champion recipe from 14775 to 15246; a lens that adds zero and a missing gear score identically to no lens; earlier reference scores are identical. A bug of 0.79 in how she flattened her words is fixed and now has a direct test. Stated limits: she has not yet placed a winning lens herself; gears are extracted by a Python tool when she is built, only from her own program, only register-only ones. Documentation is in Spanish.

Janax es un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador escritos a mano en assembler, hechos para alojar a Razar. v0.83: los engranajes — un programa se desarticula en las piezas que repite, y Luma las usa como lentes de su ojo en las recetas que escribe. Prototipo de investigación.
